ce_bugs.text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:15 — The credential-sync endpoint's Fetch Response is returned as if it were every provider's existing token result, so the new endpoint cannot satisfy Google and HubSpot's incompatible response contracts.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97 — The safe-parse result object is persisted as the credential key instead of its parsed data, so the next credential load cannot satisfy the Google credential schema.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:105 — After refreshing and storing a new Salesforce token, the new connection is still initialized with the stale credential token, so the immediate request uses an expired token.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:3 — The shared refresh helper returns either a fetch Response or an arbitrary provider SDK result, so its untyped boundary makes sync mode incompatible with callers such as HubSpot that expect a parsed token object.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:94 — Credential-sync refresh returns a Fetch Response but this path reads `res.data`, so an expired Google credential falls back to the stale token after a TypeError.

packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:177 — Credential-sync refresh returns a Fetch Response rather than a HubSpot token object, so the refresh stores unusable fields and never sets a usable access token.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:101 — The newly refreshed Salesforce token is persisted but the constructed connection still uses the pre-refresh access token, causing requests to fail whenever that stored token is expired.
apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:25 — An unset webhook secret makes an omitted header authenticate because both values are undefined.

mrv_findings.text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:94 — `const token = res?.data;` — sync returns a native Response without `.data`, so Google credential refresh throws.

packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:177 — `const hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken = await refreshOAuthTokens(...);` — sync returns a native Response instead of a HubSpot token, so undefined fields are persisted or used.
packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8 — `[z.string().toString()]: z.number(),` — computed keys become `"[object Object]"`, so expiry requirements are not validated.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75 — `const response = await fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token", {` — Salesforce bypasses the new credential-sync endpoint, leaving that supported integration stale when sync is enabled.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97 — `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` — the Zod `{ success, data }` envelope is persisted as the credential key, corrupting the next refresh.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:86 — `const res = await refreshOAuthTokens(...); const token = res?.data;` — the shared-credential branch returns native fetch Response, so Google refresh fails with undefined token data.

packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:177 — `const hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken = await refreshOAuthTokens(...);` — native Response output is treated as a HubSpot token and yields an invalid credential.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:5 — `[z.string().toString()]: z.number(), [z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional(),` — overwritten literal keys accept incompatible responses and permit non-refreshable credentials to be stored.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:25 — `req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` — an unset secret makes a headerless unauthenticated request pass and write arbitrary users’ credentials.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/decodeOAuthState.ts:9 — `const state: IntegrationOAuthCallbackState = JSON.parse(req.query.state);` — unsigned, session-unbound OAuth state permits forged callback context and account-linking CSRF.
